questions.q: When did Nehemiah give his brother Hanani charge over Jerusalem?
questions.a: Nehemiah gave Hanani charge of Jerusalem after he (Nehemiah) had finished the wall, set up the doors, and appointed the gatekeepers, singers, and Levites.

questions.q: When were the gates of Jerusalem supposed to be opened?
questions.a: The gates were supposed to be opened when the sun became hot.

questions.q: Although the city was wide and large, were there people and houses within it?
questions.a: There were few people within the city, and no built houses.

questions.q: What did God put into Nehemiah’s heart to do?
questions.a: God put into Nehemiah’s heart to gather together the nobles, the prefects, and the people to be enrolled by genealogy.

questions.q: What was done concerning the priests who could not find their genealogical records? What did the Tirshatha restrict them from doing?
questions.a: The priests who could not find their genealogical records were desecrated from the priesthood. The Tirshatha said that they should not be allowed to eat the holy food from the sacrifices until a priest stood with Urim and Thummim.

questions.q: What was done concerning the priests who could not find their genealogical records? What did the Tirshatha restrict them from doing?
questions.a: The priests who could not find their genealogical records were desecrated from the priesthood. The Tirshatha said they should not be allowed to eat the priest’s share of food from the sacrifices.

questions.q: When might the priests who could not prove their genealogy be included in the priesthood again?
questions.a: They might be included when there was a priest to stand with Urim and Thummim.

questions.q: How many people were counted in the enrollment of the assembly?
questions.a: The whole assembly was counted to be 42,360 people.

questions.q: Who gave gifts for the work?
questions.a: Some of the heads of ancestors’ families gave gifts, as did both the Tirshatha and the rest of the people.

questions.q: When did the priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, temple servants, and people live in their cities?
questions.a: They lived in their cities by the seventh month.

commentary.text: Register of those that first returned.

Verses 1–4 Nehemiah, having finished the wall, returned to the Persian court, and came to Jerusalem again with a new commission. The public safety depends on every one's care to guard himself and his family against sin.

Nehemiah knew that the safety of a city, under God, depends more upon the inhabitants than upon its walls. Every good gift and every good work are from above. God gives knowledge, he gives grace; all is of him, and therefore all must be to him. What is done by human prudence, must be ascribed to the direction of Divine Providence. But woe to those who turn back from the Lord, loving this present world! and happy those who dedicate themselves, and their substance, to his service and glory!
